g.text: The `UInt32` lexeme as a finite automaton (`languages/src/turing.rs:139`)
Every radix lane has the SAME shape, because the source
pattern repeats the same idiom four times: one digit,
then any number of *optionally-separated* further digits.
self-loop, which is exactly why `1_u32` and `1__0u32`
are rejected. `_1u32` is rejected for the mirror reason:
The suffix sits OUTSIDE the alternation group in the source
pattern, so it is mandatory for every radix. That is what keeps
the surface `q0` unambiguous: `0` alone is not a `UInt32` lexeme,
so `q0` can only be the nullary constructor `Q0`, never the
indexed former `Q` applied to a literal.
A leading `0` is genuinely shared: the same character begins the
decimal literal `0u32` and each of the radix prefixes `0b` / `0o` /
`0x`. One character of lookahead resolves it, and this is the only
place in the token class that needs any.
